title: PROMPTS improves pregnant women’s knowledge and reported care in Kenya
summary: Women at Kenyan facilities that introduced PROMPTS, a text-message platform whose helpdesk sorts questions automatically, had improvements of 0.06–0.09 standard deviations across five measures.
account: Researchers studied PROMPTS at 40 Kenyan health facilities. The platform combined health information, reminders, and a helpdesk that classified questions for automated replies or clinical review. The trial enrolled 6,139 pregnant women between November and December 2021 and followed them through August 2022. Women at facilities assigned to introduce PROMPTS had improvements of 0.06–0.09 standard deviations across five measures of knowledge, preparation, and reported care. Care-seeking for danger signs did not improve significantly. The trial evaluated the whole platform and was not powered for clinical outcomes. The natural-language processing system changed during this period: the technical paper dates the deployment of TRIM-AI to June 2022. Jacaranda Health reported cumulative reach of 3,580,095 mothers across 23 Kenyan counties and 1,500 facilities during July–September 2025. Talk Africa reported on 13 October 2026 from Bungoma County that a first-time mother found that the messages taught her about nutrition and danger signs. In the same report Victor Barasa, a doctor at Malindi Sub-County Hospital, cautioned against overreliance on automated systems and said that doctors must use their own clinical judgment. Jacaranda Health's head of programs told the reporter that some mothers have no phone or cannot read Kiswahili.
purpose: Deliver pregnancy and postpartum information by SMS and triage incoming questions to a clinical helpdesk by intent and priority.
system: PROMPTS, an SMS health platform with automated message classification and a clinical helpdesk; TRIM-AI was introduced in June 2022
deployer: Jacaranda Health with Kenyan county health facilities
location: Eight counties (Kajiado, Kilifi, Kirinyaga, Kisii, Meru, Narok, Nyeri, Siaya), Kenya
taxonomy_note: The trial measured health knowledge and reported care practices, not clinical outcomes.

ratings.reason: Women had measurable improvements in knowledge and reported care practices.

ai_role.statement: The helpdesk classified questions and directed messages to automated responses or clinicians. The trial evaluated the whole platform, so the NLP system’s separate effect was not measured.
